item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Best Replacement Has 11,000+ ‘Very Positive’ Reviews on Steam
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was released last week, nearly three decades after the original came to Nintendo 64. Plenty of newcomers are discovering the greatest game ever for the first time (raises hand) on Nintendo Switch 2 . However, as it’s a Switch 2 exclusive, plenty of gamers might be left feeling like Squidward watching everyone else have fun and frolic in Hyrule.

item.title: Every Legend of Zelda Game, Ranked
item.description: Created by the great Shigeru Miyamoto in the 1980s as an expression of his childhood love of exploring without a map, Zelda has always held a revered position in gaming culture, although it never quite enjoyed popular success to match — not, that is, until its unlikely rebirth in 2017, thanks to the runaway success of the Nintendo Switch and the revolutionary design of Breath of the Wild .

item.title: What is the Business Scrub password in Zelda Ocarina of Time?
item.description: Getting the Business Scrub password in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is one of the trickier side quests you can tackle. It involves a bit of time travel, which means finding the password is something you can't do until roughly the middle of the game. However, it's worth the trouble, as the entrepreneurial little scrub has a very important item for you.

item.title: Even More Free DLC for Hollow Knight: Silksong Might Be on the Way
item.description: After approximately 100 years of waiting, Hollow Knight: Silksong was released last fall. Players were eager to jump into it as Silksong hit a peak of nearly 600,000 concurrent players on Steam alone. Critics adored it too as Silksong was nominated for several end-of-year awards and won a handful of them, such as Best Action/Adventure Game at The Game Awards . Around that time, Team Cherry announced it was working on a new Silksong expansion called Sea of Sorrow .

item.title: A Major 2027 Pokémon TCG Change Could Be Bad News For Everyone
item.description: Being a Pokémon Trading Card Game fan is tough on wallets. Major retailers like Target and Walmart charge more than the manufacturer's retail price; stores like Best Buy, which stick to MSRP, are extremely competitive. Increased vendor prices and extraordinary resale price gouging are pushing more card shops to sell TCG products for or above market rates. And now, Pokémon fans are starting to fear that the hobby's pricing is about to get even worse across the board.

item.title: James Gunn's DCU Is Officially Dead, and That's Good News for Superman Fans
item.description: A popular online joke format in recent months goes something like this: If James Gunn had been in charge of the Marvel Cinematic Universe , what would his first three movies have been?

item.title: Warhammer’s Brutal Fantasy Football Game Just Suffered Another Setback
item.description: Warhammer fans will have to wait a little longer to return to the fantasy football pitch, but the upcoming overhaul is bringing some welcome additions. Warhammer Blood Bowl has been delayed into early 2027, pushing the game's full release out of its previously planned 2026 launch window. Publisher Slitherine announced the delay during its Dominion Days showcase in Berlin, explaining that additional development time is needed to deliver a more polished experience.

item.title: All carpenter locations in Gerudo Fortress in Zelda Ocarina of Time
item.description: The Gerudo guards captured four carpenters at Gerudo Fortress in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and it's Link's job to rescue them. By heading west of Hyrule Field , you will enter Gerudo Valley. If you cross the broken bridge — which you can do by riding Epona — you can talk to the Master Craftsman, who will ask Link to help his apprentices by sneaking into the fortress and releasing them.

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Scarier Than Ever on Switch 2
item.description: When I first encountered The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time growing up, it scared the crap out of me. The screeching Redeads, the skittering spiders, the disembodied hands — it was basically a horror movie to a young kid’s eyes. I’m older and harder to spook now, of course, which means that I knew the Nintendo 64 game’s fresh Switch 2 remake was bound to hit differently. Surely I’d laugh at everything that used to creep me out and realize that I was scared of a glorified cartoon!
